I farm only 5 mu, and at my age I will keep this year simple and steady. I have grown cotton for 50 years, so I will stay with cotton on all 5 mu instead of trying anything new. Because I have well irrigation, I can manage water myself, so I am willing to use improved seed and put in a moderate fertilizer program to protect yield without overspending. I will plough before planting because that is the field preparation I trust most for cotton here, and it helps me get a clean seedbed at the start of the season. I will irrigate a few key times rather than too often, because cotton does not need heavy watering all season, but I do not want drought stress at establishment, flowering, and boll setting. I will use pesticides only as needed but I expect several applications over the season because cotton usually faces insect pressure. My goal is a stable harvest and manageable fieldwork for my household, not chasing the highest possible output.
